strengths: Novel statistical analysis identifying spectral properties (low-frequency bias and few-mode bias) essential for video VAE diffusability, with principled mathematical foundations via Wiener-Khinchin theorem
Strong theoretical contribution: Theorem 1 elegantly connects VAE latent eigenspectra to diffusion model learning dynamics, providing genuine mechanistic insight into convergence acceleration
Lightweight and practical methods (LCR and LMR) that are computationally efficient, backbone-agnostic, and easily implementable without modifying diffusion training pipelines
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (VBench, MovieGenBench, MovieValid), resolutions, and model scales with rigorous ablation studies showing complementary effects
Significant practical improvements: 3× convergence speedup with 1.3B model outperforms 4B baseline, and consistent ~10% reward gains across diverse settings
Well-written paper with clear motivation, effective visualizations, and sufficient implementation details for reproducibility; supplementary material is thorough
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual techniques: LCR is conceptually simple (local correlation encouragement), and LMR resembles existing masked reconstruction approaches (MAEtok, DC-AE-1.5); novelty resides primarily in analysis and combination rather than techniques

Reconstruction-generation trade-off inadequately explored: Table 2 shows degraded reconstruction metrics (PSNR 37.51 vs. 39.30, LPIPS 0.0339 vs. 0.0206 vs. Wan 2.2), but implications and acceptable boundaries are not systematically analyzed

Theorem 1's generalizability uncertain: theory assumes flow-matching with velocity prediction, but applicability to other diffusion formulations (epsilon/x-prediction) is not validated; non-monotonic relationship in Eq. 3 lacks intuitive explanation

Incomplete temporal analysis: while LCR claims temporal advantages, the 3D DCT analysis is brief and visual; rigorous temporal frequency characterization and quantitative comparison of temporal vs. spatial contributions are missing

Evaluation limitations: heavy reliance on UnifiedReward (reward model-based), inconsistent FVD improvements (sometimes worse: SSVAE FVD 828 vs. Wan 2.2 FVD 733 at 17×512×512), and absence of human evaluation studies and statistical significance tests

Hyperparameter complexity underplayed: LCR (α, ω) and LMR (mask ratios/probabilities) have multiple hyperparameters; supplementary analysis of sensitivity exists, but implications for practitioners adapting to new architectures/datasets are unclear

Insufficient discussion of limitations and failure modes: no analysis of scenarios where spectral biasing hurts performance, when reconstruction trade-offs become unacceptable, or generalization to image generation and other domains
FMB and decoder robustness mechanisms entangled in LMR: Table 3 shows both matter, but relative contributions are not clearly quantified; unclear which benefit drives the observed improvements

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the reconstruction-generation quality mismatch in latent diffusion models
Principled statistical analysis examining latent space properties from complementary perspectives (spatio-temporal frequency and channel eigenspectrum)
Theorem 1 provides theoretical insight connecting VAE eigenspectrum to diffusion model learning dynamics via cross-correlation analysis
Practical, lightweight regularizers (LCR and LMR) that are computationally efficient and backbone-agnostic
Extensive experiments across multiple backbones, model scales, resolutions, and datasets with thorough ablation studies
Strong empirical results showing 3× convergence speedup and consistent improvements on multiple benchmarks
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of spectral properties
weaknesses: Limited novelty of core contributions: low-frequency bias extends known results from SER [20] incrementally, and masked reconstruction closely resembles existing approaches (MAEtok, DC-AE-1.5)
Weak causal link between analysis and methods despite criticism of prior work for same issue—LCR and LMR do not directly optimize the identified spectral properties but use proxies
Reconstruction quality regression not adequately justified: SSVAE LPIPS 0.0339 vs. Wan 2.2 0.0206 (~65% worse) dismissed as 'slight' without justification
Experimental methodology concerns: custom 48-channel baseline VAE and non-standard training setup (6:7 image-video ratio) make fair comparison with published methods difficult

Heavy reliance on internal MovieValid dataset (non-reproducible) and learned UnifiedReward model for best results; FVD often contradicts reward improvements, and no human evaluation validates reward model alignment

Theorem 1 has limited practical relevance: assumes linear networks, based on deep linear network framework [19] with known limitations, and doesn't rigorously connect to observed convergence acceleration
Significant hyperparameter sensitivity: Table 5 shows UR ranging 39.0–42.9 across mask configurations; choices (α=0.75, ω=0.02) appear empirically optimized without principled justification
Principal component analysis justification arbitrary: no ablation justifying channel-wise PCA over spatial or temporal decomposition
Incomplete comparisons: DC-AE-1.5 only in Fig. 7, no full generation comparison with SER and VA-VAE
Generalization unclear: all experiments on text-to-video with ResNet-based 3D VAEs; unclear if findings transfer to image VAEs or other architectures
Statistical rigor lacking: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; presumably single runs
Evaluation heavily concentrated on internal datasets; public benchmark improvements (VBench, MovieGenBench) more modest than reported headline gains

strengths: Strong statistical foundation: First principled direct analysis of video VAE latent spaces for diffusion training, moving beyond proxy metrics to actionable design targets

Novel theoretical contribution: Theorem 1 elegantly connects VAE latent eigenspectrum to diffusion training dynamics via cross-correlation, providing mechanistic insight into why few-mode bias accelerates convergence
Complementary spectral perspective: Unified framework identifying two synergistic spectral properties (low-frequency bias and few-mode bias), overcoming limitations of prior isolated analyses
Practical lightweight methods: Both LCR and LMR are simple, computationally efficient, and backbone-agnostic, requiring no modifications to existing diffusion training pipelines

Comprehensive experimental validation: Thorough evaluation across resolutions (256-512×512), scales (0.75B-4B), datasets (VBench, MovieGenBench, MovieValid), and backbones (MMDiT, Wan) with consistent 3× convergence speedup and 10% reward gains
Rigorous reproducibility: Extensive hyperparameter ablations (Tables 3-5), detailed implementation details, supplementary analysis, and promised code release
Clear presentation: Well-motivated problem statement, effective visualizations, and comprehensive supplementary material
weaknesses: Theoretical scope limitations: Theorem 1 assumes flow-matching with velocity prediction; generalization to other diffusion formulations (DDPM, EDM) unclear. Cross-correlation analysis builds on linear network theory, but validity for nonlinear diffusion models not rigorously justified

Underexplored reconstruction trade-off: Table 2 shows SSVAE LPIPS (0.0339) substantially worse than Wan 2.2 (0.0206), contradicting claims of comparable reconstruction. Impact of this trade-off and conditions under which it is acceptable need deeper analysis

Empirical design choices lack full justification: Patch size (2), masking ratios {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75}, and selection probabilities {0.7, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1} appear empirically optimized rather than theoretically motivated; limited principled derivation

Evaluation methodology concerns: Heavy reliance on learned UnifiedReward model without human evaluation studies; inconsistent FVD improvements (Table 1: SSVAE 983 > Wan 2.2 873 on VBench 17×256×256) suggest metric sensitivity and potential learned model bias

Limited applicability analysis: Table 4 shows LCR improvements 'less pronounced in low-channel VAEs,' indicating limited benefit for already-optimized small models. Scalability to much larger VAEs and alternative architectures (Vision Transformers) unclear

Incomplete mechanism analysis: Decoder robustness enhancement through LMR described intuitively (masking as noise injection) but not formally analyzed. Why FMB particularly helps longer sequences (Fig. 1) deserves deeper investigation

Missing comparisons and ablations: No analysis of combining LCR with existing frequency-biasing methods (SER, VA-VAE); limited comparison with concurrent work (DC-AE-1.5); unclear why decoder finetuning helps covariance-penalized baseline but not LMR variant (Table 3)

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the reconstruction-generation trade-off in VAEs, with 'diffusability' as a novel actionable design objective
Rigorous experimental validation: extensive comparisons across resolutions, frame counts, model scales; 1,200-pair human study (55.7% win rate); public data validation ruling out internal bias
Comprehensive theoretical analysis: Theorem 1 connecting VAE latent eigenspectra to diffusion training dynamics; cross-correlation view providing intuition for FMB acceleration
Complementary spectral analyses revealing that existing methods (SER, foundation-model alignment) promote low-frequency bias, yielding new insights into their effectiveness
Practical solutions with negligible computational overhead (<1.2 ms total) that are lightweight, backbone-agnostic, and easy to integrate
Strong empirical results: 3× convergence speedup, SSVAE 1.3B outperforms Wan 2.2 VAE 4B with 67.5% fewer parameters, consistent improvements across diverse settings
Thorough ablations isolating contributions of individual components and reconstruction quality analysis showing smooth latents compatible with high fidelity
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: Theorem 1 is a straightforward eigenvalue relationship in linear systems; practical implications rely heavily on empirical mode strength analysis rather than fundamental principles

Incremental contributions: FMB is expected from dimensionality; low-frequency bias extends SER [23] to spatio-temporal domain; LMR adapts MAEtok to latent space. Main novelty is combining existing insights

LCR justification is hand-wavy: jump from Wiener-Khinchin theorem to local patch correlation approximating small-lag autocorrelation lacks rigor; patch size (2) appears arbitrary with limited sensitivity analysis
Reconstruction-generation trade-off not systematically explored: LMR causes 0.23 PSNR degradation; no principled analysis of trade-off boundaries or whether further optimization is possible

Theorem 1 has limited scope: applies only to flow-matching with velocity prediction; assumption that diffusion models learn each eigenmode independently is implicit and unjustified; breaks under ε-prediction
Evaluation limitations: heavy reliance on reward models despite justification; FVD 'mixed at 256p' suggests method works better in specific regimes without analysis; no failure case documentation

Generalization questions: all experiments on text-to-video; unclear if findings transfer to other modalities or tasks; limited exploration of channel counts; sensitivity to diffusion hyperparameters unexplored
Hyperparameter sensitivity: introduces new hyperparameters (α, ω for LCR; mask ratios for LMR); aggressive settings can degrade performance (Table A.3); no principled selection method

Presentation issues: 'diffusability' never formally defined; relationship between FMB and low-frequency bias not explained conceptually upfront; dense exposition with key insights buried; small figures
Missing key comparisons: DC-AE-1.5 not in main results (Table 1); no comparison with simply training longer/on more data; limited comparison with concurrent spectral regularization methods

strengths: Systematic statistical analysis of video VAE latent spaces with clear identification of two beneficial spectral properties (few-mode bias and low-frequency bias)
Novel connection via cross-correlation analysis (Theorem 1) linking VAE latent structure to diffusion training dynamics
Practical regularizers (LMR, LCR) that are lightweight, backbone-agnostic, and add negligible computational overhead
Comprehensive experimental validation: multiple diffusion backbones, scales (0.75B-4B), metrics (reward models prioritized over FVD), ablations, and public dataset validation
Strong human preference study (55.7% win rate in 1,200-pair evaluation) aligning with reward model improvements
Clear reproducibility efforts with detailed hyperparameters and extensive supplementary diagnostics
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty: few-mode bias and low-frequency regularization are established concepts; the main contribution is combining them via cross-correlation analysis, which is incremental for practitioners familiar with diffusion models
Theorem 1 applies only to flow-matching with velocity prediction, limiting scope; the result is a straightforward consequence of linear transformation properties and doesn't extend to ε-prediction

Mixed experimental results undermine main claims: FVD degradation at 256×256 (909→983), reconstruction quality drop (0.23 dB PSNR), and only improvements at higher resolutions—contradicting 'consistent improvement' claims

Unfair experimental comparisons: re-trained baselines differ from official models; 48-channel SSVAE compared against methods with different architectures/capacities; internal MovieValid dataset used for VAE training limits generalizability
Incomplete mechanistic understanding: paper identifies what helps (few modes, low frequencies) but not why; cross-correlation analysis shows correlation with convergence, not deep causal mechanism

Generalization concerns: all VAE training uses proprietary internal dataset; only diffusion training validated on public data; no evidence of transfer to other video domains or out-of-distribution content

Design choices lack justification: LMR mask ratios appear arbitrary; LCR patch size=2 is extreme with no ablation; batch-level vs. per-sample correlation justification weak; cosine similarity choice only for 'stability'
Missing key direct comparisons with most relevant prior work (SER [23] on frequency biasing; limited DC-AE-1.5 [6] comparison); most comparisons use different architectures confounding results
'3× speedup' claim ambiguous: Figure 1 shows iteration count improvement, not wall-clock time; unclear whether this accounts for VAE training overhead and experimental variability
Statistical rigor lacking: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multi-seed results despite high variance in diffusion training; claims rely on single runs

Reconstruction vs. generation trade-off downplayed: 0.23 dB PSNR drop present; argument that 'diffusion noise reduces importance' is hand-wavy given existing methods achieve both high reconstruction and smooth latents naturally
Overstated terminology and claims: 'diffusability' is non-standard; 'first detailed statistical analysis' overclaimed; 'consistent outperforming' not supported uniformly (especially FVD results)

strengths: Novel statistical analysis identifying two complementary spectral properties (few-mode bias and low-frequency bias) crucial for video VAE diffusability, addressing the overlooked reconstruction-vs-generation trade-off

Theorem 1 provides elegant theoretical connection between VAE latent eigenspectrum and diffusion training dynamics via cross-correlation analysis, offering more direct mechanistic insight than prior proxy-metric approaches
Two lightweight, practical, and backbone-agnostic regularizers (LMR and LCR) with negligible computational overhead (1.1 & 0.6 ms) that are easy to implement and integrate

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple resolutions (256×256, 512×512, 81×256×256), datasets (VBench, MovieGenBench, MovieValid, public data), model scales (0.75B-4B), and metrics (UnifiedReward, VideoAlign, FVD)
Strong empirical results: 3× convergence speedup, 10% video reward improvement, 1.3B SSVAE outperforms 4B Wan 2.2 VAE with 67.5% fewer parameters, validated by 1,200-pair human study (55.7% win rate)
Thorough ablation studies examining component interactions, hyperparameter sensitivity, comparison with alternatives (CPR), and public data validation to rule out training bias

Clear presentation with well-motivated progression from channel spectrum to frequency spectrum analysis, insightful connections explaining why prior methods (SER, VA-VAE) work, and comprehensive supplementary material
weaknesses: Theorem 1's theoretical scope is limited to flow-matching with velocity prediction; ε-prediction doesn't exhibit same property, reducing generality across diffusion parameterizations and limiting understanding of mechanism

Reconstruction quality trade-off: LMR reduces PSNR by 0.23 dB vs. baseline, and SSVAE (37.84 dB) underperforms Wan 2.2 (39.30 dB) and IV-VAE (40.29 dB), suggesting decoder robustness and reconstruction trade-off may not be fully resolved
Inconsistent FVD results (worse at 256×256 resolution) suggest reward model improvements may not be across-the-board; requires discussion of metric disagreement and possible generation artifacts

Hyperparameter sensitivity: LCR threshold α requires careful tuning with performance degradation when over-biased (Fig. A.5), and LMR mask ratios show sensitivity (Tab. A.4), suggesting method isn't entirely plug-and-play

Evaluation fairness concerns: SSVAE trained for 200k steps vs. likely longer official Wan 2.2 training; while re-trained baselines help, comparisons still potentially favor proposed method; user study on internal MovieGenBench data

Limited generalization analysis: focus exclusively on text-to-video generation with no exploration of image-to-video, video editing, or other diffusion tasks; unclear if spectral properties generalize to different architectures

Incomplete theoretical explanation for why smooth latents intrinsically help diffusion models; cross-correlation analysis explains mode strengths but not fundamental reasons diffusion can't adapt to handle non-smooth latents

Spatio-temporal frequency analysis feels less thorough than spatial: LCR uses uniform patch size (2) without ablation on spatio-temporal patch ratios; limited separation of temporal vs. spatial low-frequency contributions
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals reported; some improvements modest (1-2 points on certain metrics), and it's unclear if results would hold with larger sample sizes
